originalTitle: Shein valued at $26bn after long-awaited stock market debut
summary: The firm's Hong Kong listing on Tuesday comes after a years-long quest to sell shares in New York and London.
content:
Shein's founder Xu Yangtian, right, and the firm's financial director Poppy Bao at the Hong Kong Stock Exchange

Ultra-fast-fashion brand Shein has been valued at $26.2bn (£19.3bn) after its first day of public trading, following a long quest to list on the stock market.

The company was once estimated to be worth nearly $100bn, but has faced heated competition, trade tensions and questions over the ethics of its supply chain.

Shein's share price fell in the early hours of trading but recovered ground before closing down just 0.12%.

The company's attempts to list in the UK and US were scuppered after supply chain concerns and criticism of its environmental impact.

On Monday, Shein priced its shares at HK$48.56 each, raising ‌13.6 billion Hong Kong dollars ($1.7bn; £1.3bn) from the listing.

That gave the company a stock market valuation of $26.3bn.

Shein's shares fell by as much as 10% in early trading before the losses eased. They closed at $48.50, leaving it valued at $26.15bn.

Shein became hugely popular , especially among younger people, due to its ability to source the very latest fashions at ultra-low prices through a vast network of factories in China .

At a ceremony to celebrate the listing, chief financial officer Leigh Gui said the company's model of selling large numbers of small orders with rapid payment options now reaches about 160 markets worldwide.

"Let global consumers enjoy the sound of fashion," he said after a gong was struck to mark the start of trading.

Shein has more than 273 million active customers who placed a total of more than a billion orders in the year to the end of March 2026, the firm said in a filing ahead of the listing .

But it now faces higher costs, regulatory scrutiny and more competition, said Charu Chanana, chief investment strategist at Saxo.

For customers, the slump in Shein's shares is a sign that the firm's cheap prices are "becoming harder to sustain", which may lead to higher prices, she added.

The listing marks the largest new share sale in Hong Kong so far this year, which is being seen as a test of investor appetite for the fast-fashion industry.

It is a rare "standalone" e-commerce firm that can be assessed on its own merits, fashion industry analyst Louise Deglise-Favre from research firm GlobalData.

Shares in rivals Asos and Boohoo have been battered in recent years as they face regulatory scrutiny and fierce competition.

"Investors have learned to be sceptical," while concerns over sustainability and ethical issues add to the complexity of Shein's share sale, Deglise-Favre said.

The rise and rise of fashion giant Shein

The truth behind your $12 dress: Inside the Chinese factories fuelling Shein's success

Founded in China and headquartered in Singapore since 2021, Shein has spent several years touting its credentials as a global company, but ultimately was forced to return to its Asian roots to go public.

The company once looked set for one of the largest stock market debuts ever by a Chinese firm, with Wall Street in its sights.

The firm's long road to the stock market highlights the geopolitical pressures and regulatory scrutiny faced by Chinese companies with global ambitions.

Its business had surged during the Covid-19 pandemic as people, stuck at home, turned to online retailers. At the same time, social media influencers shared their hauls for millions of followers to see.

Shein faced resistance from US lawmakers, who objected to the planned listing over concerns of forced labour in its factories. In response to such allegations, the company has said it takes a "zero-tolerance policy for forced labour".

An initial public offering (IPO) in the US - by far Shein's largest market - would have offered it a chance to further increase its global profile and tap into Western financing.

It has also been accused of copying other designers' ideas. Shein has said "it takes all claims of infringement seriously" and that it respects the rights of all designers.

Shein also explored the possibility of making its stock market debut in London but faced similar opposition.

The BBC has contacted Shein for further comment.

In 2025, Shein shifted its attention to Hong Kong, with Chinese authorities approving the move in July this year.

"Shein ran out of venues that could take it," said Ashley Dudarenok, founder of Chinese market research firm ChoZan.

The company attempted to "look less Chinese" by shifting its headquarters to Singapore ahead of its IPO bid, but it never won political backing abroad nor assurances from Beijing, she added.

Shein is backed by a vast network of factories in China

Trade tensions and regulatory concerns mean Shein is navigating a very different landscape to when it first started exploring a potential IPO.

In July, it reported a $99m quarterly loss as its sales slowed after the US struck down an import duty exemption on small packages.

The exemption, known as the de minimis rule , had helped Shein and rival Temu grow rapidly as it allowed packages worth less than $800 to enter the US without incurring import duties.

Similarly, the European Union has imposed a €3 (£2.57; $3.50) tax on low-value imports.

The Iran war has also hit demand, raised costs and caused delays to deliveries in some markets, Shein has said.

Shein's fast-fashion model has come under scrutiny over its environmental impact

Its rivals are feeling the pressure too. In August, Temu-owner PDD reported lower-than-expected quarterly revenue.

The company also needs to find ways to stand out from its rivals, that are now also using predictive technology to make their websites more appealing to shoppers, said Jason Hsu from Rayliant Global Advisors.

"Shein is no longer a unique player," Hsu said.

Shein is also being investigated by US and European regulators over its business practices.

chineseTitle: 期待已久的 Shein 首次上市后估值达 260 亿美元
chineseSummary: 该公司多年来一直寻求在纽约和伦敦出售股票，随后于周二在香港上市。
chineseContent:
Shein创始人徐扬天（右）和公司财务总监Poppy Bao在香港证券交易所

超快时尚品牌 Shein 经过长期寻求上市，上市首日后估值达 262 亿美元（193 亿英镑）。

该公司的估值曾一度估计接近 1000 亿美元，但目前面临着激烈的竞争、贸易紧张局势以及供应链道德问题。

Shein 股价在早盘交易中下跌，但在收盘前收复失地，仅下跌 0.12%。

由于供应链问题和对其环境影响的批评，该公司在英国和美国上市的尝试失败了。

周一，Shein 将其股票定价为每股 48.56 港元，通过上市筹集了 136 亿港元（17 亿美元；13 亿英镑）。

这使得该公司的股票市场估值达到 263 亿美元。

Shein 的股价在早盘交易中下跌了 10%，之后损失有所缓解。收盘价为 48.50 美元，市值为 261.5 亿美元。

Shein 非常受欢迎，尤其是在年轻人中，因为它能够通过中国庞大的工厂网络以超低的价格采购最新的时装。

在庆祝上市的仪式上，首席财务官Leigh Gui表示，该公司以快速付款方式销售大量小订单的模式现已覆盖全球约160个市场。

“让全球消费者享受时尚之声”，在交易开始的锣声敲响后，他说道。

该公司在上市前提交的一份文件中表示，Shein 拥有超过 2.73 亿活跃客户，截至 2026 年 3 月底的一年内，其下达订单总数超过 10 亿份。

盛宝银行首席投资策略师查鲁·查纳纳表示，但它现在面临着更高的成本、监管审查和更激烈的竞争。

她补充说，对于客户来说，Shein 股价的暴跌表明该公司的廉价价格“变得越来越难以维持”，这可能会导致价格上涨。

此次上市标志着今年迄今为止香港最大的新股发行，这被视为对投资者对快时尚行业兴趣的考验。

研究公司 GlobalData 的时尚行业分析师 Louise Deglise-Favre 表示，这是一家罕见的“独立”电子商务公司，可以根据自身优点进行评估。

近年来，由于面临监管审查和激烈竞争，竞争对手 Asos 和 Boohoo 的股价遭受重创。

Deglise-Favre 表示，“投资者已经学会了保持怀疑”，而对可持续性和道德问题的担忧则增加了 Shein 股票出售的复杂性。

时尚巨头Shein的崛起与崛起

12 美元裙子背后的真相：助推 Shein 成功的中国工厂内部

Shein 自 2021 年在中国成立、总部设在新加坡，多年来一直宣扬其作为一家全球公司的资质，但最终被迫回归亚洲根源进行上市。

该公司一度有望成为中国公司有史以来规模最大的股票上市之一，并将目光投向华尔街。

该公司漫长的上市之路凸显了雄心勃勃的中国企业所面临的地缘政治压力和监管审查。

在 Covid-19 大流行期间，由于困在家里的人们转向在线零售商，该公司的业务激增。与此同时，社交媒体影响者分享了他们的成果，供数百万粉丝观看。

Shein 面临美国立法者的抵制，他们因担心其工厂存在强迫劳动而反对计划上市。针对此类指控，该公司表示采取“对强迫劳动的零容忍政策”。

在美国（Shein 迄今为止最大的市场）进行首次公开​​募股（IPO）将为其提供进一步提高其全球形象并利用西方融资的机会。

它还被指控抄袭其他设计师的想法。 Shein 表示“公司严肃对待所有侵权索赔”，并尊重所有设计师的权利。

Shein 还探讨了在伦敦股市首次亮相的可能性，但也面临着类似的反对。

BBC 已联系 Shein 寻求进一步评论。

2025年，Shein将注意力转向香港，并于今年7月获得中国当局批准。

中国市场研究公司 ChoZan 的创始人阿什利·杜达雷诺克 (Ashley Dudarenok) 表示：“Shein 没有足够的场地来容纳它。”

她补充说，该公司试图在首次公开募股之前将总部迁至新加坡，以“看起来不那么中国化”，但它从未赢得国外的政治支持，也从未赢得北京的保证。

Shein 得到中国庞大工厂网络的支持

贸易紧张局势和监管担忧意味着 Shein 正在面临与刚开始探索潜在 IPO 时截然不同的局面。

7 月份，该公司公布季度亏损 9900 万美元，原因是美国取消小包装进口关税豁免后其销售放缓。

这项被称为最低限度规则的豁免帮助 Shein 和竞争对手 Temu 迅速发展，因为它允许价值低于 800 美元的包裹进入美国而无需缴纳进口关税。

同样，欧盟对低价值进口产品征收 3 欧元（2.57 英镑；3.50 美元）的税。

谢因表示，伊朗战争也打击了需求，提高了成本，并导致一些市场的交货延迟。

Shein 的快时尚模式因其对环境的影响而受到审查

它的竞争对手也感受到了压力。 8 月份，Temu 所有者 PDD 公布的季度收入低于预期。

Rayliant Global Advisors 的 Jason Hsu 表示，该公司还需要找到从竞争对手中脱颖而出的方法，这些竞争对手现在也在使用预测技术来提高其网站对购物者的吸引力。

“Shein 不再是一个独特的球员，”Hsu 说。

Shein 还因其商业行为而受到美国和欧洲监管机构的调查。

随着“最低限度”关税豁免结束，美国购物者将受到怎样的打击
